stem.text: An open-top baking pan is made from a rectangular sheet of tin 45 inches by 72 inches by cutting a square of side x from each corner and folding up the sides. The baking pan can be at most 2 inches tall. Find the largest possible volume of the baking pan, in cubic inches.

worked_solution.text: The baking pan has height x and a base \( 45 - 2 x \) by \( 72 - 2 x \), so its volume is \( V(x) = x\left(45 - 2 x\right)\left(72 - 2 x\right) \).
The cut must be positive, less than half the sheet, and at most 2, so the domain is \( 0 < x \le 2 \).
\( V'(x) = 12 \left(x - 30\right) \left(x - 9\right) \), which is zero at \( x = 9 \) and \( x = 30 \); only \( x = 9 \) lies strictly inside the sheet.
The critical point \( x = 9 \) is beyond the height limit, and \( V'(x) > 0 \) for every x in \( 0 < x \le 2 \), so V is increasing there and is largest at the right endpoint \( x = 2 \).
The largest volume is \( V(2) = 2\left(41\right)\left(68\right) = 5576 \) cubic inches.

options.derivation: the shorter side of the base at the optimum reported instead of the volume
the height limit left out of the domain, so the critical point x = 9 is used
the side of the cut square, where the maximum occurs, reported instead of the volume
